self_critique:
The biggest problems are fixed. The hero now reads as a glowing, translucent lime gummy rather than an olive blob: colour^0.5, a lighter lime absorption, the light-linked glow and moving it in front of the stripes did most of that. The mesh is smooth candy instead of lumpy glass. The bonk is legible: the gap closes on screen, there is a dent, and the ball rolls back. After the bonk every beat carries motion until a clean f166 hold. The floor falls off toward the bottom, the contact shadows ground the blocks, and the circle match, lock, whip and static QA all still pass.

Where it is still weak:
- The critic's numeric light targets are only partly met. p5 is 0.51, not <= 0.40, and the gummy's own shadow is faint. A translucent lime gummy can't throw a dark contact shadow without a much harder key, and I didn't push that against the toy-softbox brief.
- The frame stays high-key pink overall. The floor reads pink-cream because it reflects the walls, and the lower-left corner leans mauve.
- About 10-19% of the gummy shows bright orange refracted blush stripes. That is the refraction proof working, but a purist may still call parts of the body yellow-orange.
- The critic's 45-degree key spread was rejected after measurement: Cycles conserves power when spread narrows, so it concentrated the key and washed the coral out. The overhead key plus cutter flag does that job instead.
- I did not A/B clamp_indirect, did not render the f104-115 final strip, and the cost estimate rests on a few idle frames because GPU 6 was heavily shared late in the session.

rejected_critic_items: Issue 1, KEY spread 45 deg aimed at T_LOCK: rejected after measurement. Cycles keeps an area light's power constant as spread narrows, so 45 deg concentrated the key; even at 120 W the coral rendered #FA8078 and the floor salmon. I moved the key over the set and added a horizontal cutter flag instead, which gives the front-floor falloff without touching the coral.

Issue 1, the 2x1 m flag between key and front floor: replaced. From the front-left 3.2 m key that flag printed an elliptical blob, and a wide one blocked the whole key, because near a large softbox the rays to every target bundle together. The overhead key plus a horizontal cutter at z 2.4 separates the front-floor rays from the action.
Issue 1, fill x0.5: used x0.7 with a lavender tint. The fill is what lights the stripe wall behind the gummy (the gummy's backlight); at x0.5 the stripes went mauve-grey (lead G2).
Issue 1, floor albedo cream x0.7: used x0.85. At x0.7 cream reads beige/tan, which G2 forbids.

Issue 1/2, a plain top-back SPOT: implemented instead as a light-linked AREA glow whose only receiver is the gummy (lead note 1 mandates light linking). An unlinked spot floods the floor and erases its reflections (r1 finding).
Issue 2, surface TINT 0.35 (mix white-lime): the lead's colour^0.5 (G5) takes priority, applied to a pre-compensated #A0E61D. Density about 2 -> 1.6 and no mint were applied.
Issue 3, Subdivision Surface modifier after the lattice: not added. Taubin smoothing removed the crinkle, and per-frame subdivision would add BVH and deformation-blur cost against the G4 cap.
Issue 3, roughness 0.12: used 0.10, because 0.12 blurs the refracted stripes, one of the four proof paths.
Issue 3, the final strip f104-115 with qa_diff: not run for lack of time; the lead's f31-42 strip was done and measured.
